newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Air Afrique states meet, debt deadline looms.
newsitem.headline: Air Afrique states meet, debt deadline looms.

text.p: Air Afrique member states met in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan on Monday to choose a new boss for the struggling multinational carrier with a debt repayment deadline looming.

Five heads of state attended the meeting, which will choose a replacement for Frenchman Yves-Roland Billecart, whose mandate was cut short by the 11 member states. Billecart's job, chairman and managing director, will be split between two people.

Host president, Ivory Coast's Henri Konan Bedie, told the meeting draconian measures would be needed to ensure a lasting recovery of the airline, which serves West and Central Africa but also Europe, the United States and South Africa.

"First we must take all the necessary steps to ensure the (airline's) capacity to make significant (debt) repayments," Bedie said, noting that it had to pay 31 billion CFA in arrears by the end of December 1996.

He also called for recapitalisation of the airline, which has debts of around $400 million but lacks the operating revenue to ensure regular repayment. The debt relates to airliners bought soon after Billecart took over in 1989.
The 1994 devaluation of the CFA franc used in many French-speaking countries in Africa also undermined the airline's ability to repay its U.S. dollar-denominated debt.

Air Afrique, based in Abidjan, is majority owned by Benin, Burkina Faso, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Ivory Coast, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Senegal and Togo. Air France and other third parties also have a stake.
